Weekly Lessons

Week after week,

further in.

Aaron teaches guitar and ukulele in weekly sessions — one hour, one person, outdoors on Maui. Guitar or ukulele, any starting point. Each week picks up where the last one ended, and the pace is set by the student, not a syllabus.

People who keep coming back describe a shift that's hard to predict at the start — the progress becomes noticeable, the hour becomes something they protect. At some point the lesson stops feeling like practice and becomes the part of the week they most look forward to: the one where showing up and staying curious is the whole job.

ABOUT AARON

CHAPTER 1 OF 4

Early Years

Aaron has been teaching guitar and ukulele on Maui for years — working with complete beginners and returning players to help them find their footing. Aaron began his journey in music education over two decades ago. While studying at Illinois State University, he explored guitar, piano, and music theory, discovering a love for collaboration and live performance.

Most first-time students leave playing a complete song.

Music Lessons on Maui FAQ
Do I need experience before taking a music lesson on Maui?

No. Aaron teaches complete beginners, returning players, families, couples, and weekly students. Lessons start with your current comfort level and focus on playing music right away.

Do I need to bring a ukulele?

Ukuleles can be borrowed for lessons when needed. Guitar students should mention whether they have an instrument when requesting a lesson time.

How far in advance should I book?

Aaron books 2–3 days ahead. If you have a specific date in mind, reach out early — spots fill quickly during busy seasons.

What will I actually learn in one lesson?

In a single session, most students leave able to play a complete song — chords, strumming pattern, and all. Aaron starts where you are and keeps it musical from the first few minutes.

What if I need to cancel or reschedule?

Aaron is flexible. If your plans change, just reach out as early as you can and he'll work with you.
